mainTopic: A father's duties to his son (פדיון הבן and teaching תורה), which מצוה comes first, and learning versus marrying
overview: The amud starts by finishing a discussion about a father who must redeem both himself and his firstborn son. If he has only five סלעים, he redeems himself first. רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about a case with sold land and free land, and their argument depends on whether a debt from the תורה works like a loan in a שטר. A ברייתא then asks which comes first, redeeming one's son or going up for the רגל. Another ברייתא teaches that every son who is his mother's first child must be redeemed. The גמרא next gives the source for a father's duty to teach his son תורה, and a chain of פסוקים showing that women are not obligated to learn or teach. When father and son both need to learn, the father usually comes first, and this is shown through the story of רב אחא בר יעקב and the demon in אביי's study hall. The amud ends by asking whether to learn תורה or marry first, with stories and sayings stressing early marriage. רב חסדא's statement about marrying at sixteen continues on the next amud.

steps.title: With only five סלעים, the father redeems himself first
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that if there are only five סלעים, the father's own redemption comes before his son's, because a מצוה on his own body is preferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever there are only five סלעים, he comes before his son. Why? Because a מצוה that is on his own body is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement about what everyone agrees on. When there is only enough money for one פדיון, the father redeems himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a man who was never redeemed by his own father, and now he also has a בכור son. Both redemptions are his responsibility, but there is only enough money for one. His own מצוה, the one that is about his own body, wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Silver coins. Five of them are the price of redeeming a firstborn son.
A מצוה that is on his own body, his personal obligation

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא אֶלָּא חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים –
phrases.english: Anywhere that there are only five sela,
phrases.notes: Five סלעים is enough to redeem only one person, either the father or the son.

phrases.english: he takes precedence over his son.
What is the reason?
A מצוה of his own body is preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא אֶלָּא חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the statement of agreement that began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With only five סלעים, the father redeems himself before his son, because his own מצוה comes first.

steps.title: Where the disagreement really is
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is only in a case with five סלעים of liened, sold land and five סלעים of free land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is when there are five סלעים worth of liened property and five worth of free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly which case רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about. This sets up the explanations of each side in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liened property (משועבדים) is land the man already sold, but an earlier creditor can still collect from it. Free property (בני חורין) is land he still owns, with no claims on it. The question becomes which debt can be collected from which land.

keyTerms.meaning: Liened property: land that was sold but can still be collected by an earlier creditor
Free property: land still owned, with no lien on it

phrases.english: When they disagree is where
there is five [sela worth] of liened property
phrases.notes: This is land he already sold to someone else.

phrases.english: and five [sela worth] of unsold property.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא חָמֵשׁ מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the disagreement to a specific case, now that the case everyone agrees on is set aside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement is only where there is both liened land and free land.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a תורה debt is like a written loan, so both can be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a debt from the תורה is like a loan written in a שטר, so the כהן can collect from sold land. The father uses the free land for his son, and the כהן collects the father's redemption from the sold land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that a loan written in the תורה is like one written in a document. So with these five free סלעים he redeems his son, and the כהן goes and collects the five liened סלעים for the father's own redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה lets the son be redeemed first: done this way, both מצוות get done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan written in a שטר can be collected even from land sold after the loan began. The father's own redemption debt began when he was born, before the land was sold, so the כהן can collect it from the sold land. The son's debt began only after the sale, so it must be paid from the free land.

keyTerms.meaning: A debt that comes from the תורה (like פדיון הבכור)
Like a loan written in a legal document
Collects or seizes land from a buyer to pay a debt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
a loan that is written in the Torah
phrases.notes: Some versions say דכתיב (in round brackets); the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Both mean 'written'.

phrases.english: is considered like one written in a document,
with these five he redeems his son,
phrases.notes: 'These five' means the free land.

phrases.english: and the priest goes and repossesses
the five of liened property for him [the father].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's reasoning for the case defined in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תורה debt is like a written loan, so the son is redeemed with the free land and the כהן collects the father's redemption from the sold land.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a מלוה הכתובה בתורה is or is not like a written loan comes up in other places in ש״ס too.

steps.title: The רבנן: a תורה debt is not like a written loan, so the father comes first
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that a debt from the תורה cannot be collected from sold land, so only the free land is available, and the father's own מצוה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that a loan written in the תורה is not like one written in a document, and therefore his own מצוה is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's reasoning: since the sold land can't be used at all, they are back to the basic rule from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a תורה debt can't be collected from sold land, then only the five free סלעים count. That is the same as having only five סלעים, so the father redeems himself.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן depends on one question: can a debt that comes from the תורה be collected from sold land, the way a loan written in a שטר can?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
a loan that is written in the Torah
is not considered like one written in a document,
and therefore his own מצוה is preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי מִלְוָה דִּכְתִיב בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָאו כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה's reasoning in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תורה debt is not like a written loan, so only the free land counts and the father redeems himself first.

steps.title: ברייתא: redeem your son first, then go up for the רגל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a person must both redeem his son and go up to ירושלים for the רגל, the first opinion says he redeems his son first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if he needs to redeem his son and to go up for the festival, he redeems his son and afterward goes up for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about another clash between two מצוות. Here the first opinion (the תנא קמא) gives priority to פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who has enough money for only one of the two מצוות. The first opinion says redeeming the son comes first, and going up for the רגל comes after.

keyTerms.meaning: To go up to ירושלים for a festival

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
[If he has] to redeem his son and to go up for the festival,
phrases.notes: He means he only has enough money for one of the two.

phrases.english: he redeems his son
and afterward goes up for the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן לִפְדּוֹת אֶת בְּנוֹ וְלַעֲלוֹת לָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case about putting מצוות in order, after the father-versus-son discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion says פדיון הבן comes before עלייה לרגל.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the רגל comes first because its time passes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says to go up for the רגל first, because that מצוה's time passes, while redeeming the son can still be done later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he goes up for the festival and afterward redeems his son, because this one is a מצוה that passes, and that one is a מצוה that does not pass.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and explains why: a מצוה with a deadline should be done before one that can wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the festival is over, the chance to go up for it is gone. The obligation to redeem the son stays, so he can still do it after the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה that does not pass; it can still be done later

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's rule: when two מצוות clash, the one that will be lost if you wait comes first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלֶה לָרֶגֶל, וְאַחַר כָּךְ פּוֹדֶה אֶת בְּנוֹ.
phrases.english: he goes up for the festival, and afterward redeems his son.
For this is a מצוה that passes,
phrases.notes: 'This' is going up for the רגל.

phrases.english: and this is a מצוה that does not pass.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עוֹלֶה לָרֶגֶל וְאַחַר כָּךְ פּוֹדֶה אֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עלייה לרגל comes first because it is a מצוה עוברת, while פדיון הבן can wait.

steps.title: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יהודה already gave his reason, and asks for the source of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand רבי יהודה, because he told us his reason. But what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן say to redeem the son before going up for the רגל. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה explained himself: the רגל has a set time and will pass, but פדיון הבן can still be done later. The רבנן gave no reason, so the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
it is as he stated his reason.
But the Rabbis, what is their reason?
phrases.notes: This is the first opinion from step 5, which says to redeem the son first.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה כִּדְקָאָמַר טַעְמָא אֶלָּא רַבָּנַן מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first opinion of the ברייתא, since רבי יהודה's reason was already given in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic for the רבנן's ruling that פדיון הבן comes before עליה לרגל.

steps.title: The order of the verse puts redeeming first
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from the order of the פסוק: redeeming the firstborn is written first, and appearing at the רגל comes after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, "All the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem," and only after that it says, "None shall appear before Me empty."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn the order of the מצוות from the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מצוות are in one פסוק, and redeeming the firstborn is mentioned before going up to ירושלים. The רבנן read that order as telling us which מצוה comes first. רבי יהודה instead decides by which מצוה's time will run out.

keyTerms.meaning: Empty-handed (coming to the רגל without a קרבן)

phrases.english: For the verse says:
"All the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem,"
phrases.notes: שמות 34:20

phrases.english: and then: "None shall appear before Me empty."
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק, and it is talking about going up to ירושלים for the רגל.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn it from the order of the פסוק: redeeming the firstborn is written before appearing at the רגל.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: go to the רגל first, because its time passes. רבנן: redeem the son first, because the פסוק lists it first.

steps.title: Five firstborn sons from five wives must all be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man with five sons, each the first child of a different wife, must redeem all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How do we know that if a man had five sons from five wives, he must redeem all of them? The פסוק says, "All the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It says that every son who is the first child of his mother needs פדיון, even when the father has several of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each son is the first child his own mother had. The word "כל" (all) in the פסוק teaches that the father must redeem every one of them, not just one.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From where do we know that if he had
five sons from five wives,
phrases.notes: Each son is the very first child of his own mother.

phrases.english: that he must redeem all of them?
The verse teaches:
"All the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם הָיוּ לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה בָּנִים מֵחָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא that uses the same פסוק, "כל בכור בניך תפדה".
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every son who is the first child of his mother needs פדיון, so a man with five such sons from five wives redeems all five.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the תורה already ties the מצוה to opening the womb, so of course each mother's first son is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! The תורה made the מצוה depend on being the first to open the mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא is teaching something we already know, so it seems to need no פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah defines the firstborn as the one who opens the womb, each of the five sons qualifies through his own mother. The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to bring a special word to teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who opens the womb (the mother's first child)
The תורה made it depend on

phrases.english: It's obvious!
The Torah made it depend on opening the womb!
phrases.notes: See שמות 13:2. Each of these sons opened his own mother's womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא בְּפֶטֶר רֶחֶם תְּלָא רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for a פסוק to teach that all five sons are redeemed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah already ties firstborn status to the mother, so each son clearly qualifies without any extra teaching.

steps.title: We might have compared it to the firstborn of inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that without the ברייתא we might have learned from inheritance, where the firstborn is counted by the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us learn "firstborn" here from "firstborn" in inheritance. Just as there it means "the first of his strength," so too here it means "the first of his strength." So the ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows there was a real mistake we could have made, so the ברייתא was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For inheritance, the firstborn who gets a double portion is "ראשית אונו", the father's first son. Using the same word "בכור", we might have said only the father's first son needs פדיון. The ברייתא teaches that for פדיון we count by the mother, so all five are redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)
Let us learn (one case from another)
The first of his strength (the father's first son)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of בכור. For inheritance, we count by the father's first son. For פדיון הבן, we count by the mother's first child.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Let us learn "firstborn" and "firstborn" from inheritance,
just as there it means "the first of his strength,"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17. There it means the father's first son.

phrases.english: so too here it means "the first of his strength,"
so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא נֵילַף בְּכוֹר בְּכוֹר מִנַּחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a possible mistake (מהו דתימא) that the ברייתא prevents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Compare פדיון to inheritance through the shared word "בכור", so only the father's first son would need פדיון.
steps.terutzMaskana: For פדיון we count by the mother, so every son who is the first child of his mother must be redeemed.
steps.whatToRemember: פדיון הבן follows the mother (פטר רחם). Inheritance follows the father (ראשית אונו).

steps.title: Where do we learn the duty to teach one's son תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next obligation of a father listed in the ברייתא, teaching his son תורה, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said a father must teach his son תורה. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the next item in the list of a father's obligations and asks where it comes from. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, the גמרא went through the father's duties one at a time. Now it turns to teaching תורה and looks for a פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: To teach him Torah.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְלַמְּדוֹ תּוֹרָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of the father's obligations and starts a new item.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that obligates a father to teach his son תורה.

steps.title: The verse: you shall teach them to your sons
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק "ולמדתם אותם את בניכם".
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And you shall teach them to your sons."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that clearly tells fathers to teach their children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "ולִמַּדתם" means "you shall teach," and it is said directly about "your sons." This makes teaching תורה a duty of the father.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And you shall teach them to your sons."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:19

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וְלִמַּדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.

steps.title: If the father did not teach him, he must teach himself
steps.stepSummary: If the father did not teach his son, the son must learn on his own. This is learned by reading the same word as "וּלְמַדתם", meaning "you shall learn."
steps.simpleTranslation: If his father did not teach him, he must teach himself, as it is written "וּלְמַדתם", meaning "you shall learn."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new rule. The duty to learn תורה does not end just because the father did not do his part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same letters can be read with different vowels: "וְלִמַּדתם" (you shall teach) or "וּלְמַדתם" (you shall learn). The second reading puts a duty on each person to learn for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall learn (the second way of reading the word)

steps.whyThisMatters: Learning תורה is not only the father's duty. Every person who was not taught must learn by himself.

phrases.english: And where his father did not teach him,
he is obligated to teach himself,
as it is written: "And you shall learn."
phrases.notes: It is the same word in the פסוק, just read with different vowels: "you shall learn" instead of "you shall teach."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא דְּלָא אַגְמְרֵיהּ אֲבוּהּ מִיחַיַּיב אִיהוּ לְמִיגְמַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule from the same פסוק, read with different vowels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person whose father did not teach him תורה must learn it himself, based on reading the word as "ולמדתם".

steps.title: Why a mother is not obligated to teach her son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a mother is not obligated to teach her son תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that a woman is not obligated to teach her son תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה said women are exempt from the duties a father has toward his son, and teaching him תורה is one of those duties. Now the גמרא asks how we know the mother is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source in step 13 said 'teach your sons' but did not say who must do the teaching. So the גמרא asks why only the father is obligated.

phrases.english: She — from where do we know that she is not obligated?
phrases.notes: 'She' is the mother, and the question is about teaching her son תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהִי מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the father's duty to the mother's exemption
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a mother is exempt from teaching her son תורה

steps.title: Only one who must learn must teach
steps.stepSummary: From the two readings of ולמדתם, the גמרא links teaching to learning: whoever must learn must teach, and a woman, who does not have to learn, does not have to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word can be read 'you shall teach' and also 'you shall learn.' So whoever is commanded to learn is commanded to teach, and whoever is not commanded to learn is not commanded to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same double reading from step 14. It joins the duty to teach to the duty to learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one word in two ways puts both duties in one word, so they go together. A woman is not commanded to learn תורה, so she is not commanded to teach it either. Why she is not commanded to learn is asked in the next step.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall teach,' which can be read 'and you shall learn,'
whoever is commanded to learn is commanded to teach,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה לִלְמוֹד – אֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה לְלַמֵּד.
phrases.english: and whoever is not commanded to learn is not commanded to teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְלִימַּדְתֶּם״ ״וּלְמַדְתֶּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Teaching depends on being obligated to learn, and a woman is not obligated to learn

steps.title: Why a woman is not obligated to learn herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know a woman is not obligated to teach herself תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that she is not obligated to teach herself?
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer depended on a woman not being obligated to learn. Now the גמרא asks for the source of that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 rests on an idea that has not been proven yet. This question goes back to fill that gap.

phrases.english: And she, from where do we know
that she is not obligated to teach herself?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיהִי מְנָלַן דְּלָא מִיחַיְּיבָה לְמֵילַף נַפְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the idea that step 16 relied on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a woman is not obligated to learn תורה herself

steps.title: Whoever others must teach must teach himself
steps.stepSummary: Using the same double reading, the גמרא links learning yourself to being taught by others: only someone others must teach must teach himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word can be read 'you shall teach' and 'you shall learn.' So whoever others are commanded to teach must teach himself, and whoever others are not commanded to teach does not have to teach himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same double reading again, this time to tie self-learning to being taught by others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the link is between 'others must teach you' and 'you must learn on your own.' If others are not commanded to teach a woman, she is not commanded to teach herself. The גמרא still has to prove that others are not commanded to teach her.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall teach,' which can be read 'and you shall learn,'
whoever others are commanded to teach
is commanded to teach himself,
and whoever others are not commanded to teach
is not commanded to teach himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְלִימַּדְתֶּם״ ״וּלְמַדְתֶּם״, כֹּל שֶׁאֲחֵרִים מְצֻוִּוין לְלַמְּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Self-learning is required only of someone whom others are commanded to teach

steps.title: Why others are not commanded to teach a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that others are not commanded to teach a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that others are not commanded to teach her?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 18 rested on one more idea, so the גמרא asks for its source. This is the last link in the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer so far has rested on an idea that was not yet proven. This question reaches the bottom of the chain, which needs a direct פסוק.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that others are not commanded to teach her?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין אֲחֵרִים מְצֻוִּוין לְלַמְּדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the idea that step 18 relied on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that there is no duty to teach a woman תורה

steps.title: Your sons and not your daughters
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'your sons,' which teaches that the duty is to teach sons and not daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And you shall teach them to your sons.' This means your sons, and not your daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the base of the whole chain: the פסוק itself says 'your sons.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the duty to teach is only toward sons, nobody is commanded to teach a daughter. Then, by step 18, she does not have to teach herself. And by step 16, she does not have to teach her son.
steps.whatToRemember: The chain runs backward: the פסוק says sons, not daughters → no one must teach a woman → she does not have to learn herself → she does not have to teach her son.

phrases.english: As the verse says: 'And you shall teach them to your sons'
phrases.notes: דברים 11:19

phrases.english: Your sons, and not your daughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְלִמַּדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 and finishes the chain
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'your sons' leaves out daughters

steps.title: Father and son both need to learn: the father comes first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a father and his son both need to learn, the father comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he needs to learn and his son needs to learn, he comes before his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא for the case where there are not enough resources for both father and son to learn. The first opinion says the father comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father has two duties, to learn himself and to teach his son. When he cannot do both, this view puts his own learning first.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
He needs to learn and his son needs to learn
phrases.notes: He can only pay for one of them to learn.

phrases.english: he comes before his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא לִלְמוֹד וּבְנוֹ לִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא on the order of the duties to learn and to teach
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's own learning comes before his son's

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a sharp son comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the son is diligent, sharp, and remembers his learning, the son comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If his son is diligent and sharp, and his learning stays with him, his son comes before him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in one kind of case: a son who is very talented.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees the father usually comes first. But if the son will succeed more in learning, the family's chance to learn should go to the son.

keyTerms.meaning: stays with him; he remembers it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If his son is diligent and sharp
and his learning stays with him,
his son comes before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם בְּנוֹ זָרִיז וּמְמוּלָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the תנא קמא in the case of a gifted son
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A diligent, sharp son whose learning lasts comes before his father

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב decides to go learn himself
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב אחא בר יעקב sent his son to אביי. When he saw the son was not sharp, he decided to go learn himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב יעקב, son of רב אחא בר יעקב. His father sent him to אביי. When he came back, the father saw that his learning was not sharp. He said to him: I am better than you. You stay here, so that I can go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case showing the ברייתא in action. The son was not sharp, so the father took the chance to learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the ברייתא: since the son was not 'diligent and sharp,' רבי יהודה's exception did not apply, and the father came first. The father first tried sending the son, then switched after he saw the result.

phrases.english: Like this story of Rav Yaakov,
son of Rav Acha bar Yaakov:
his father sent him before Abaye.
When he came back, he saw him
that his learning was not sharp.
He said to him: I am better than you,
you stay here, so that I can go.
phrases.notes: Literally 'sit.' The son stays home and takes care of things while the father goes to learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יַעֲקֹב בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the ברייתא with a real case
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a father comes first when the son is not especially sharp
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אחא בר יעקב and his son

steps.title: אביי plans for a miracle against the demon
steps.stepSummary: אביי heard that רב אחא בר יעקב was coming. Since a dangerous demon was in his study hall, אביי told people not to host him, hoping a miracle would happen through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי heard that he was coming. There was a certain demon in אביי's study hall. When people entered even two at a time, even by day, they were harmed. אביי said to them: No one should give him a place to stay. Perhaps a miracle will happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues and sets up the next part. אביי arranges for רב אחא to sleep in the study hall, hoping his merit will defeat the demon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon was so dangerous that even two people together, in daytime, were hurt. Without a place to stay, רב אחא would have to sleep in the study hall. אביי hoped a great צדיק would bring a miracle, and how it turns out is told in the next part.

phrases.english: Abaye heard that he was coming.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the father, רב אחא בר יעקב.

phrases.english: There was a certain demon
in the study hall of Abaye,
that when people would enter, even two together,
even by day, they would be harmed.
He said to them: Let no one give him
a place to stay,
phrases.notes: Read this with the row before it: 'let no one give him a place to stay.' That way he'd have to sleep in the study hall.

phrases.english: perhaps a miracle will happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע אַבָּיֵי דְּקָא הֲוָה אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב אחא בר יעקב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: אביי sets things up so that רב אחא will face the demon, hoping for a miracle

steps.title: The Miracle in the Study Hall
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב sleeps in the study hall, a seven-headed demon appears, and each time he bows one head falls off. The next day he tells the townspeople they put him in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went in and slept in that study hall. The demon looked to him like a snake with seven heads. Every time he bowed, one of its heads fell off. The next day he told them: If a miracle had not happened, you would have put me in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story from the last step. אביי's plan worked, and the demon was destroyed through רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, אביי told people not to host רב אחא so he would have to sleep in the study hall. Here we see the result: a miracle happens and the demon is killed. רב אחא's words show he knew the danger was real and that the townspeople had risked his life.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall, literally 'the house of the Rabbis'

phrases.english: He entered and spent the night in that study hall.
It appeared to him like a serpent
with seven heads.
With every bow that he bowed,
one of its heads fell off.
He said to them the next day:
If a miracle had not happened,
you would have put me in danger.
phrases.notes: He is speaking to the townspeople who refused to host him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָל, בָּת בְּהָהוּא בֵּי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in steps 23-24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through רב אחא בר יעקב's merit, a miracle happened and the demon was destroyed.

steps.title: Learn Torah First, Then Marry
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person should learn תורה first and marry afterward. But if he cannot manage without a wife, he should marry first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If a person needs to learn תורה and also to marry, he should learn תורה first and then marry. But if he cannot be without a wife, he should marry first and then learn תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: which comes first, learning תורה or getting married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of setting priorities in learning, like the father-and-son question earlier. The basic rule is תורה first, but there is a clear exception for someone who cannot manage without a wife.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he needs to study Torah and to marry a woman,
he should study Torah
and afterward marry a woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ בְּלֹא אִשָּׁה –
phrases.english: And if it is impossible for him to be without a wife,
he should marry a woman
and afterward study Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה וְלִישָּׂא אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new priority question after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learn תורה first and then marry, unless he cannot manage without a wife.

steps.title: שמואל Rules: Marry First
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה is to marry first and then learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is that a person marries and afterward learns תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the practical ruling: marriage comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא made 'marry first' only an exception. שמואל makes it the normal rule for everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not just repeating the exception in the ברייתא. He makes marrying first the standard practice.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The law is: one marries a woman
and afterward studies Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is to marry first, then learn תורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: A Millstone Around the Neck
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks how a person can learn תורה with a millstone around his neck, meaning the burden of supporting a family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: With a millstone around his neck, can he really be busy with תורה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view: a married man is too burdened to learn well, so learning should come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words are phrased as a question, but they work as a strong opinion. They seem to clash with שמואל's ruling and set up the גמרא's answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A millstone around his neck,
phrases.notes: The millstone is a picture of the heavy job of supporting a wife and family.

phrases.english: and he should engage in Torah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: רֵיחַיִים בְּצַוָּארוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a view that seems to oppose שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A married man is too weighed down to learn properly, so learning comes first.

steps.title: No Argument: Each Speaks to a Different Place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל and רבי יוחנן do not really disagree. One speaks to 'us' and the other to 'them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not argue: this one is for us, and that one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash between שמואל and רבי יוחנן by saying each one speaks about different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of picking one side, the גמרא says both are right in their own setting. 'Us' means the people of בבל, and 'them' means the people of ארץ ישראל. The best order depends on the living situation of the people involved.

keyTerms.meaning: This is for us and that is for them

steps.whatToRemember: Whether to marry first or learn first depends on the place and situation. שמואל and רבי יוחנן each speak to a different community.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this is for us, and that is for them.
phrases.notes: 'Us' means the learners in בבל and 'them' means those in ארץ ישראל. Each opinion fits one of these places.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: הָא – לַן, וְהָא – לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent argument between steps 27 and 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל and רבי יוחנן truly argue about what comes first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each opinion applies to a different community, so there is no real argument.

steps.title: רב הונא Rebukes the Unmarried רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא praises רב המנונא to רב הונא. When רב הונא sees that רב המנונא does not wear a head covering because he is unmarried, he turns away and tells him not to come back until he marries.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא praised רב המנונא to רב הונא, saying he was a great man. רב הונא said: When he comes to you, bring him to me. When he came, רב הונא saw that he did not wear a head cloth. He asked him: Why don't you wear a head cloth? He answered: Because I am not married. רב הונא turned his face away from him and said: See that you do not see my face until you marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how seriously רב הונא, a sage of בבל, took the need for a תלמיד חכם to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a 'great man' was turned away for not being married. This fits שמואל's ruling for בבל that one marries first. The head cloth was worn by married scholars, so wearing none showed he was single.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreads a head cloth over his head

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how strongly the sages of בבל felt that marriage should not be delayed, even for a great scholar.

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁתַּבַּח לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda would praise to Rav Huna
Rav Hamnuna, saying that he is a great man.
He said to him: When he comes to you,
bring him to me.
When he came, he saw him
that he did not spread a cloth over his head.
phrases.notes: This head cloth was worn by married scholars, so not wearing one showed he was single.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason
that you do not spread a head cloth?
He said to him: Because I am not married.
He turned his face away from him.
He said to him: See that you do not see
my face until you marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁתַּבַּח לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הוּנָא בִּדְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the 'marry first' approach used in בבל.
steps.raayaObject: The importance of marrying early, as the sages of בבל practiced it. The גמרא right away ties this story to רב הונא's own view (step 31).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב הונא and רב המנונא

steps.title: רב הונא's view: unmarried at twenty means a life of sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's reaction to רב המנונא matches his known statement that a man unmarried at twenty spends all his days in sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא is following his own opinion, because he said: a man who is twenty years old and has not married spends all his days in sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links the story we just saw to a general rule רב הונא taught elsewhere. He was so strict with רב המנונא because he holds that staying single past twenty leads to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לטעמיה tells us this is not a one-time reaction. It is part of רב הונא's consistent position. His wording, 'all his days in sin,' is very strong, and the גמרא will question it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his known view

phrases.english: Rav Huna follows his own reasoning
phrases.notes: This explains why רב הונא turned away from רב המנונא in the previous story.

phrases.english: for he said:
one who is twenty years old
and has not married a woman,
all his days are in sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב הונא's behavior in the story of step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who reaches twenty without marrying spends all his days in sin.

steps.title: Can it really mean he is in sin all his days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a single man cannot literally be called sinful for his whole life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think he is in actual sin all his days?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on how strong רב הונא's words sound. It cannot be that every unmarried man is actually sinning all the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge targets the literal meaning of 'בעבירה.' Being unmarried does not automatically mean a person commits sins. The wording therefore needs to be read differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a phrase that rejects an impossible reading)

phrases.english: In sin? Can that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲבֵירָה סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal wording of רב הונא's statement in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'כל ימיו בעבירה' in רב הונא's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being unmarried does not mean a person actually commits sin his whole life, so the literal reading is impossible.

steps.title: Correction: all his days in thoughts of sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the statement: the unmarried man is troubled by sinful thoughts all his days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: all his days are spent in thoughts of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by changing the wording. רב הונא meant that the man will be bothered by improper thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was not sinful actions but sinful thoughts. A man who does not marry young grows used to these thoughts, and they can stay with him even later. This keeps רב הונא's warning serious but realistic.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
all his days are in thoughts of sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 by changing the reading of רב הונא's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא seemed to say the unmarried man actually sins all his days.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means the man is troubled by thoughts of sin all his days.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's warning about not marrying by twenty is about sinful thoughts, not actual sinful acts.

steps.title: רבא's support from the school of רבי ישמעאל: God waits until twenty
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל: הקדוש ברוך הוא waits for a man to marry until twenty, and after that curses him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same thing. Until twenty years, הקדוש ברוך הוא sits and waits for a person, asking when he will marry. Once he reaches twenty and has not married, God says: 'Let his bones swell.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב הונא's idea that twenty is the deadline for marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same age, twenty, as רב הונא, so it supports his view. Before twenty God patiently waits. After twenty God curses him, which shows how serious it is to delay marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (introduces a supporting ברייתא)

phrases.english: Rava said,
and so the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Until twenty years
the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits
and waits for a person,
asking when he will marry a woman.
Once he has reached twenty
and has not married,
He says: Let his bones swell.
phrases.notes: This is a curse. It means God no longer looks after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב הונא's twenty-year deadline.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that a man should marry by twenty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל saying God waits until twenty and then curses the man who has not married.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is an important source for the idea that a man should marry by age twenty.

steps.title: רב חסדא: I am greater because I married at sixteen
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא begins explaining that he is greater than his friends because he married at sixteen, and starts to say what would have happened had he married at fourteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The reason I am greater than my friends is that I married at sixteen. And if I had married at fourteen...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a personal example of the benefit of marrying young. His sentence is not finished yet and continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא credits his early marriage for his spiritual greatness. He goes even younger than twenty, to sixteen. He then begins to imagine marrying at fourteen, and the end of his thought comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: I am superior; I am greater

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The fact that I am greater than my friends
is because I married at sixteen.
And if I had married at fourteen

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא הַאי דַּעֲדִיפְנָא מֵחַבְרַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a personal example that supports the value of marrying young.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying early, at sixteen, made רב חסדא greater than his friends.
